title: A generation's sidecar records the PROJECT's controls, not the controls the run actually used - so Reuse restores a lie
description:
generationService._snapshotControlState (js/services/generationService.js:424-460) builds the sidecar's controlState from the project's saved settings and then reconciles exactly TWO things against the run's real injectionParams: ratio and batch. Every other injected value is recorded as whatever the project happened to hold. The sidecar therefore describes a generation that did not happen, and Reuse faithfully restores it.

PROVEN LIVE 2026-08-13, both halves:
  - t2i_007 (klein-4b) was generated through POST /connector/generate with raw injection keys     Input_Style_Selector.selector=7 (Vintage) and .strength_model=0.65. The image is visibly     styled. Its sidecar records controlState.model = {styleSelect: 0, stylization: 1}. Reuse     restored Style=None, Stylization=1.00 - that card cannot be reproduced from the app.
  - t2i_006 (krea2) ran at 1k (1024x1024, correct). Its sidecar records     controlState.shared.ratioSelector.qualityTier="1k" AND controlState.model.qualityTier="2k",     because _ms (modelSettings) is cloned in wholesale and real projects carry a stale per-model     qualityTier there. After reuse the QUALITY toggle read 2K against a 1K card.

The second half is the documented stale-copy trap (js/data/projectModel.js: qualityTier is SHARED state; the modelSettings copy is leftover). agentDispatch._plannedSize already refuses to read it. The snapshot does not, so the stale value is preserved into every sidecar and handed to Reuse.

WHY IT BLOCKS MPI-547: raw injectionParams is the documented escape hatch and always wins over resolved values. Any named-parameter layer built on top inherits this unless the snapshot reconciles the keys that were actually injected. Fix the snapshot first, or MPI-547 ships generations that cannot be reused.

The existing ponytail comment above the function already names the upgrade path: snapshot from the controls' own getValue() (Flow-style), which needs a ratioSelector compound-key remap. Worth weighing against reconciling per injected key - the second is smaller but keeps the hand-maintained list the comment was trying to avoid.
